data.cultural_impact: Rehoboam, a name of Hebrew origin, holds a rich cultural significance for the Jewish and early Christian communities. The name "Rehoboam" was initially used as a symbol of power, rulership, and a wide or expansive territory owing to the meaning of the two Hebrew words. In the Bible, Rehoboam is mentioned as the third and the longest ruling king of the United Kingdom of Israel, succeeding his father, the distinguished King Solomon. Rehoboam's reign marked a departure from his father's peaceful and prosperous rule towards a more turbulent and unruly one. His rule saw the division of the kingdom of Israel into the northern and southern kingdoms. Thus, the name "Rehoboam" has had a historical impact as a symbol of leadership and territorial expansion in Jewish and Christian heritage.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Rehoboam" lies in its Hebrew meaning, conveying the idea of a wide, expansive, or spacious dwelling. In the spiritual realm, this name offers a reminder of God's boundless love and His invitation to seek refuge in Him, as cited in numerous passages of the Bible. For instance, Isaiah 32:18 offers the promise, "My people will live in peace, in quiet obedience to my name, for their own good and for the good of the earth. I will cause their enemies to vanish, and ennuity and cruel oppression will disappear." This invocation of God's expansive love and promise of dwelling at peace resonates deeply with the meaning of the name Rehoboam. Additionally, the name stands as a reminder of the spaciousness of the human soul, created in God's image, and invites one to seek spiritual growth, expansion, and transformation. Through the name, we are encouraged to broaden our spiritual horizons, deepen our connection to God, and cultivate a life of serenity and peace.

historical_references.reference: 1 Kings 12:1-24, Rehoboam is the name of the son of Solomon and the new king of Israel after Solomon's death.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Rehoboam continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

In the Old Testament, Rehoboam was the name of the son of King Solomon and successor to the throne of Israel. This name is rich in cultural and religious significance, making it an appealing choice for parents seeking a meaningful name for their child. In Christianity, Rehoboam is revered as a symbol of strength and leadership, as he went on to build up and expand the kingdom of Israel.
